Series XXIII: Pride and Progress / The Right Stuff
Series XXIII: Pride and Progress / The Right Stuff

Pride and Progress News-highlights: 1. Gay Week in Review, with Andy Humm, Joyce Hunter, Darrell Yates Rist, and Tom Stoddard 2. Discussion of particular problems homosexuals face during the holiday season, including coming out to parents, bringing partner to holiday dinner, coping with intolerant family 3. AIDS transmission outside the bloodstream, and ability to infect tissue, and the New York Times' continuing bias of male anal sex as primary method of infection 4. State's Constitutional rights in light of the Bowers v Hardwick sodomy case decision 5. Discussion of "gifts" each guest has received this year, including the strengthening of the gay community in the national spotlight COMMERCIAL: "First Hand" gay magazine 6. Andy Humm on enlightening the ignorant through vocal support for gay rights COMMERCIAL: Stamp Out AIDS featuring Jennifer Bassey 7. Hotline for latest treatments for AIDS and experimental treatments 8. Federal government's AIDS hotline becomes privatized, is expanding to 24 hours, moving to NYC 9. Lee University in Pennsylvania grants official status to a gay, lesbian, and bisexual student group 10. 62 new AIDS education PSAs used to educate average TV viewer, starring an assortment of Hollywood celebrities 11. Lesbian woman ends legal fight over her dismissal from the ROTC in 1982 12. Newly adopted Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986 continues to include language that can be used to ban gay people from entering the country 13. Philadelphia, police commissioner appoints a liaison to the gay community and commits to fully investigating complaints of anti-gay violence and hate 14. Sports Report, with clips of Greg Louganis performing a circus act 15. Closing credits
The Right Stuff: 1. This Week in History with Jeff Bixby COMMERCIAL: The Monster 2. Show Bits with George Trahanis, review of off-Broadway musical, "Have I Got a Girl for You!" COMMERCIAL: "Manscape" gay magazine 3. Michael Weyand interviews Walter Williams about his study of homosexuality in Native American culture, "The Spirit and the Flesh" COMMERCIAL: SF AIDS Foundation 4. Reminder from Razor Sharp to contact those friends who do not have families 5. $100.000 gained in an art auction to benefit five AIDS organizations in San Francisco
